summary: David W. Chappell was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. Educated at Mount Allison, McGill, and Yale, he served as a professor at the University of Hawaiʻi (~1972–2002) and taught comparative studies at Soka University of America (~2002–2004).

David W. Tien specializes in sinology and philosophy. He studied at McGill University, the University of Toronto, and the University of Michigan, completing his PhD under James Robson, and also studied under Robert H. Sharf.
David Webster is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He completed his PhD at the University of Bristol under the supervision of Peter Harvey.
Daw Ohn was a scholar of Buddhist studies and linguistics who studied at the University of Rangoon. She served there as a tutor in Pali (attested 1977).

Dawa Norbu worked in Tibetology and history. He earned degrees from the University of Delhi, St. Stephen's College, and UC Berkeley (PhD 1982), later serving as professor of Central Asian studies at Jawaharlal Nehru University (~1984–2004).
Dawa Tsering is a Tibetologist who studied under Dungkar Lobsang Thrinle. He held a post at Tibet University.

Daya Krishna was a philosopher and Indologist. He served as professor of philosophy and Pro-Vice-Chancellor at the University of Rajasthan (~1961–1984) and chaired the Indian Council of Philosophical Research (attested 1999).

Daya Ram Sahni was an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at Oriental College, the University of the Punjab, and under John Marshall. He held posts with the Archaeological Survey of India, including Deputy for Exploration (1931–1935).

Dayong was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Taixu, Bai Puren, and Palden Tenzin Nyendrak. He studied and taught at the Wuchang Buddhist Institute (1923) and founded the Tibetan Studies College.

Debala Mitra was an archaeologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Dineschandra Sircar. She served as Additional Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India from 1981 to 1983.

Debi Prasanna Pattanayak is a linguist and Indologist who studied at Cornell University (~1959–1961). He founded the Central Institute of Indian Languages, serving as its director in 1988, and chaired the Institute of Odia Studies and Research.

Debiprasad Chattopadhyaya was an Indologist and philosopher who studied at the University of Calcutta under Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan and Surendranath Dasgupta. He taught philosophy at City College, Kolkata (~1943–1983), and was a guest professor at Calcutta.

Deborah Klimburg-Salter is an art historian and Tibetologist who studied at Harvard under Oleg Grabar and at the University of Vienna. She held the Asian art history chair at Vienna (1994–2015) and taught at UCLA (1978–1985).
Declan Quigley is an Indology scholar who held teaching positions at the University of Cambridge, the University of St Andrews, and Queen's University Belfast.

Dedong Wei is a scholar of religious studies, sinology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Renmin University of China (~1995–1998), where he became an associate professor of religious studies (attested 2005).
Demchok Dorje studied under Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso and Khenpo Shenga.

Denis Sinor was a scholar of Central Asian studies, linguistics, and history. He studied under Paul Pelliot and at Cambridge, held a post at Cambridge (1948–1962), and served as a director at Indiana University (1962–1986).

Denis Twitchett was a historian and sinologist educated at SOAS and St Catharine's College, Cambridge. He held the Chair of Chinese at the University of London (1960–1968) and Cambridge (1968–1980), later becoming professor emeritus at Princeton.
Denise Bernot was a linguist who studied at the École des chartes and École des Langues Orientales. She taught at the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales from ~1960 to 1989.

Denma Lochö Rinpoche was a Buddhist scholar who studied at Drepung Loseling and Gyume Tantric Monastery under multiple traditional masters. He served as abbot of Namgyal Monastery (1986–1991) and principal of the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics.
